doc.title: Chuck Lamb interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 7, 2023

chapter: Growing up in Verona and Dry Jack
title: Mike Demicco's favor and treating people well
summary: Demicco later recommended Lamb to Chris Brubeck; both agree on professionalism, with the Aspen waiter anecdote.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Kind of a returned favor. That’s pretty neat.

That’s neat. That’s a fraternity of musicians. And I think it behooves people to know that to act professional in whatever thing you are doing because as you say, twenty years down the line some someone’s going to think —

Yes. That’s a great point. And you know if you’re playing in a jazz club and you’re cool with the staff, you know you go out of your way, “Hey man, thanks for taking care of us.” You know that dude could start running a jazz club. And that’s happened to me before, where the waiter opened up this jazz club in Aspen. He said, “Hey man can you come?” “Bill? Really, is that you?” So just what you’re saying. You know be aware of your environment, who you’re working for and just make sure you’re present. Because you don’t know.
